The root blocker session_7104685a4aac is 'idle in transaction' holding an UPDATE on inventory (product_id=1) with no blocking pids of its own — it holds row locks while waiting on the client. The full chain: d7cdae8bb9c8 -> b26e7467cb78 -> 7104685a4aac. Note the two UPDATEs target different product_ids (1 vs 2), so the blocking is likely via a shared lock path (e.g., FK or index-level contention) rather than the same row tuple; regardless, the transactionid waits are directly observed. No evidence of large data, missing indexes (PK exists), vacuum, or redundant indexes. Resolution: roll back the eligible idle-in-transaction root blocker session_7104685a4aac to release locks, preserving the business request. Uncertainty: exact mechanism by which the product_id=1 update blocks the product_id=2 update is not fully explained by the observed rows.
